neighbours.label: the position right after a mention of nitrogen, where the next token could be N (e.g. 'nitrogen (78%)')
fire: The air we breathe is mostly nitrogen (about 78%) and oxygen.
Certain bacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonia for plants.
The fertilizer label lists nitrogen (N), phosphorus and potassium.
Liquid nitrogen (at minus 196 degrees) freezes the sample instantly.
In the bond table, the triple bond in N2 is very strong.
Plants absorb nitrogen (as nitrate) through their roots.
The soil test showed low nitrogen (N) levels in the field.
Our atmosphere contains nitrogen (78 percent) plus small amounts of argon.
quiet: The air we breathe is partly oxygen (about 21%) and other gases.
Certain plants store sugar (glucose) in their roots for winter.
The fertilizer label lists calcium, magnesium and iron.
Hot water (at ninety degrees) dissolves the sugar instantly.
In the price table, the cost of bread is very low.
Plants absorb water through their roots every day.
The soil test showed high calcium levels in the field.
Our atmosphere contains oxygen (21 percent) plus small amounts of argon.

notes: Card: two top examples are '(' after 'nitrogen'; one is 'N' in a bond table; logit effect suppresses N, _N, (N, /N. Some outliers (Russian suffixes).
